these intelligent features:\n269\t\n270\t### 1. Stuck & Loop Detection\n271\t\n272\tAutomatically detect when a worker is spinning its wheels:\n273\t- No meaningful progress for N minutes\n274\t- Repeating the same tool calls (Read → Edit → Read → Edit on same file)\n275\t- Retrying failed operations repeatedly\n276\t\n277\tSurfaces problems immediately without users having to watch logs constantly.\n278\t\n279\t```\n280\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n281\t│  ⚠️  STUCK DETECTED                                                │\n282\t│                                                                     │\n283\t│  w-alpha appears stuck (same file edited 4x in 6 minutes)          │\n284\t│                                                                     │\n285\t│  Pattern detected:                                                  │\n286\t│    14:31:07  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"add validation\"                 │\n287\t│    14:33:12  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"fix validation\"                 │\n288\t│    14:35:18  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"update validation\"              │\n289\t│    14:37:24  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"refactor validation\"            │\n290\t│                                                                     │\n291\t│  Suggestion: Worker may be in a fix-break cycle                    │\n292\t│                                                      [Inspect]      │\n293\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n294\t```\n295\t\n296\t**Loop Detection Patterns:**\n297\t- Same file edited 3+ times in 5 minutes\n298\t- Same Grep/Glob pattern executed repeatedly\n299\t- Alternating Read/Edit on same file without progress\n300\t- Retry count exceeding threshold\n301\t\n302\t---\n303\t\n304\t### 2. Live Inline Diff View\n305\t\n306\tWhen a worker calls `Edit`, render the actual diff inline with syntax highlighting:\n307\t\n308\t```\n309\t14:32:07  w-alpha  INFO  Edit src/auth/login.ts\n310\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n311\t│  @@ -12,7 +12,9 @@                                                  │\n312\t│                                                                     │\n313\t│    import { User } from './types';                                  │\n314\t│                                                                     │\n315\t│  - function login() {                                               │\n316\t│  + async function login(): Promise<User> {                          │\n317\t│      const user = await authenticate();                             │\n318\t│  -   return user;                                                   │\n319\t│  +   if (!user) throw new AuthError('Invalid credentials');         │\n320\t│  +   return sanitizeUser(user);                                     │\n321\t│    }                                                                │\n322\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n323\t```\n324\t\n325\t**Implementation:**\n326\t- Parse `old_string` and `new_string` from Edit tool call logs\n327\t- Generate unified diff format\n328\t- Syntax highlight based on file extension\n329\t- Collapsible in log stream, expandable on click\n330\t\n331\t---\n332\t\n333\t### 3. Cross-Reference Hyperlinking\n334\t\n335\tEvery entity in logs becomes a clickable/navigable link:\n336\t\n337\t| Entity | Action |\n338\t|--------|--------|\n339\t| Bead ID (`bd-1847`) | Show all events across all workers for this bead |\n340\t| File path (`src/auth.ts`) | Show all operations on this file |\n341\t| Worker name (`w-alpha`) | Jump to worker detail view |\n342\t| Timestamp | Anchor link for sharing/bookmarking |\n343\t| Error code | Show all occurrences of this error |\n344\t\n345\t```\n346\tActivity Stream\n347\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n348\t│ 14:32:07  [w-alpha]  INFO  Edit [src/auth/login.ts] for [bd-1847] │\n349\t│           ─────────        ──── Worker Collision Detection\n372\t\n373\tReal-time detection when workers operate on overlapping concerns:\n374\t\n375\t```\n376\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n377\t│  ⚡ COLLISION DETECTED                                              │\n378\t│                                                                     │\n379\t│  w-alpha and w-bravo are both modifying:                           │\n380\t│                                                                     │\n381\t│  ┌───────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┐       │\n382\t│  │ File              │ w-alpha          │ w-bravo          │       │\n383\t│  ├───────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────┤       │\n384\t│  │ src/auth/login.ts │ Edit (line 45)   │ Edit (line 52)   │       │\n385\t│  │ src/auth/types.ts │ Read             │ Edit (line 12)   │       │\n386\t│  │ src/api/routes.ts │ -                │ Edit (line 88)   │       │\n387\t│  └───────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────┘       │\n388\t│                                                                     │\n389\t│  Risk: Merge conflicts, duplicated work                            │\n390\t│  Duration: Overlapping for 2m 34s                                  │\n391\t│                                                                     │\n392\t│  [View w-alpha]  [View w-bravo]  [View Diff]  [Dismiss]            │\n393\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n394\t```\n395\t\n396\t**Detection Logic:**\n397\t- Track file → worker mapping in memory\n398\t- Alert when same file has Edit from multiple workers within time window\n399\t- Severity levels: Read/Read (info), Read/Edit (warn), Edit/Edit (critical)\n400\t\n401\t---\n402\t\n403\t### 5.        (completed bd-1845)        │   │\n422\t│  │ ● w-delta    Starting  bd-1849  (just assigned)            │   │\n423\t│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n424\t│                                                                     │\n425\t│  Events at this moment:                                            │\n426\t│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n427\t│  │ ▶ 14:32:07  w-alpha   Edit src/auth/login.ts               │   │\n428\t│  │   14:32:05  w-bravo   Read src/validators/index.ts         │   │\n429\t│  │   14:32:04  w-delta   Starting task bd-1849                │   │\n430\t│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n431\t│                                                                     │\n432\t│  [j/k] Frame step  [Space] Play/Pause  [←/→] Seek  [q] Exit        │\n433\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n434\t```\n435\t\n436\t**Features:**\n437\t- Playback speeds: 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x\n438\t- Click timeline to jump to any point\n439\t- Frame-by-frame stepping (j/k or arrow keys)\n440\t- Keyboard shortcuts for common actions\n441\t- Export replay as shareable link or file\n442\t\n443\t**Implementation:**\n444\t- Events are already timestamped in logs\n445\t- Replay = render events progressively based on timestamps\n446\t- No additional storage needed\n447\t\n448\t---\n449\t\n450\t### 6.                                       │  │\n1186\t│  │  #3  2026-02-20 Session (72% match)                          │  │\n1187\t│  │      Error: Type mismatch in handler                         │ Extract error signature (type, message pattern, file pattern)\n1212\t2. Search historical session logs for similar errors\n1213\t3. Find subsequent events that resolved the error\n1214\t4. Rank by similarity and success rate\n1215\t5. Present as actionable suggestions\n1216\t\n1217\t**Error matching:**\n1218\t- Exact match: same error type and message\n1219\t- Pattern match: similar error type, related files\n1220\t- Semantic match: similar context (same task type, same module)\n1221\t\n1222\t**Feedback loop:**\n1223\t- Mark resolution as successful/failed\n1224\t- Improves future recommendations\n1225\t- Build organizational knowledge base\n1226\t\n1227\t**Why valuable:** Institutional memory. Don't repeat mistakes. Accelerate debugging. Workers (and humans) learn from past sessions.\n1228\t\n1229\t---\n1230\t\n1231\t### 18. Focus Mode with Pinning\n1232\t\n1233\tPin specific workers, tasks, or files. Everything else fades away:\n1234\t\n1235\t```\n1236\t┌─ FABRIC (Focus Mode) ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n1237\t│                                                                     │\n1238\t│  📌 Pinned: w-alpha, bd-1847                    [Exit Focus Mode]   │\n1239\t│                                                                     │\n1240\t│  ┌─ w-alpha on bd-1847 \"Implement auth flow\" ───────────────────┐  │\n1241\t│  │                                                               │  │\n1242\t│  │  Status: ● Running (8m 34s)     Cost: $1.82                  │  │\n1243\t│  │                                                               │  │\n1244\t│  │  Progress                                                     │  │\n1245\t│  │  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━●━━━━━━━━━━━━  ~70% complete       │  │\n1246\t│  │  Research → Implementation → [Testing]                        │  │\n1247\t│  │                                                               │  │\n1248\t│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n1249\t│                                                                     │\n1250\t│  Activity (filtered to pinned only)                                │\n1251\t│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n1252\t│  │                                                               │  │\n1253\t│  │  14:32:07  Edit src/auth/login.ts                            │  │\n1254\t│  │            ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │  │\n1255\t│  │            │ - function login() {                        │   │  │\n1256\t│  │            │ + async function login(): Promise<User> {   │   │  │\n1257\t│  │            └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │  │\n1258\t│  │                                                               │  │\n1259\t│  │  14:32:01  Read src/auth/types.ts                            │  │\n1260\t│  │                                                               │  │\n1261\t│  │  14:31:55  Thinking: \"Now I need to implement the token     │  │\n1262\t│  │            validation. Follow what matters. Deep focus on one task without distraction. Scales from \"show me everything\" to \"show me just this.\"\n1297\t\n1298\t---\n1299\t\n1300\t## CLI Interface\n1301\t\n1302\t```bash\n1303\t# TUI - live terminal dashboard\n1304\tfabric tui Architecture\n1320\t\n1321\t```\n1322\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n1323\t│                         FABRIC answers:** Are my workers productive? How many beads did they complete today? Which workers completed the most? Which projects got the most work done?\n1410\t\n1411\tThe live view (Phases 1–8) answers \"what is happening *right now*?\" — it shows NEEDLE state, heartbeats, active files, stuck detection. But it does not answer the retrospective question: *how much did the fleet actually accomplish?*\n1412\t\n1413\t#### The Problem\n1414\t\n1415\tWhen a user opens the dashboard and sees 40 workers all showing `EXHAUSTED_IDLE`, the dashboard appears to say \"nothing is happening.\" The correct interpretation is \"the fleet finished all available work.\" There is no way to tell from the current UI whether the workers completed 200 beads or 0.\n1416\t\n1417\tSimilarly, when workers are active, the worker card shows an event count (e.g., \"134,572 events\") but event count is an implementation detail, not a productivity signal. A worker that spent an hour stuck in a loop produces thousands of events and zero completions.\n1418\t\n1419\t#### Data Sources\n1420\t\n1421\tTwo data sources combine to answer the productivity question:\n1422\t\n1423\t**1. NEEDLE log events** (already ingested by FABRIC):\n1424\t\n1425\t| Event | What it signals |\n1426\t|-------|----------------|\n1427\t| `bead.claim.succeeded` | Worker started working on a bead; record start time |\n1428\t| `outcome.classified` with `outcome: success` | Agent exited cleanly; bead likely done |\n1429\t| `bead.released` with `reason: release_success` | NEEDLE confirmed the bead was closed; **this is the completion signal** |\n1430\t| `bead.released` with `reason: release_failure` | Worker dropped the bead without completing it |\n1431\t\n1432\tThe current `beadsCompleted` counter in `store.ts` only fires on a legacy `bead.completed` event that modern NEEDLE workers do not emit. The counter must be updated to fire on `bead.released` with `reason: release_success`.\n1433\t\n1434\t**2. Bead JSONL files** (not currently read by FABRIC):\n1435\t\n1436\tEach workspace has a `.beads/issues.jsonl` file. Closed beads carry:\n1437\t- `id` — bead identifier (prefix encodes the project, e.g. `kt-*` = kalshi-tape, `bf-*` = multi-project global)\n1438\t- `close_reason` — often contains the worker name (`\"Completed by worker claude-code-glm-4.7-india\"`)\n1439\t- `closed_at` — ISO timestamp of completion\n1440\t- `assignee` — the worker that held the bead\n1441\t\n1442\tReading these files unlocks project-level breakdown without requiring NEEDLE to emit workspace context in its log events.\n1443\t\n1444\t#### UI Changes Required\n1445\t\n1446\t**1. Fleet summary bar** (top of dashboard, always visible)\n1447\t\n1448\t```\n1449\t┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n1450\t│  3 WORKING  ·  7 SELECTING  ·  24 EXHAUSTED  ·  53 beads today  ·  0 stuck  │\n1451\t└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n1452\t```\n1453\t\n1454\tOne line. The single most important at-a-glance view. Replaces having to count individual worker cards.\n1455\t\n1456\t**2. Worker card enrichment**\n1457\t\n1458\tEach worker card should show beads completed (not event count) and, when `WORKING`, the current bead ID:\n1459\t\n1460\t```\n1461\t┌─────────────────────────────────────┐\n1462\t│  claude-code-glm-4.7-india  WORKING  │\n1463\t│  bead: bf-5r22                       │\n1464\t│  31 completed  ·  last: 2m ago       │\n1465\t└─────────────────────────────────────┘\n1466\t```\n1467\t\n1468\t**3. Worker sort order**\n1469\t\n1470\tWorkers should sort by operational importance, not alphabetically:\n1471\t1. `WORKING` (doing something right now)\n1472\t2. `SELECTING` / `CLAIMING` (about to do something)\n1473\t3. `BOOTING` / `CLOSING`\n1474\t4. `EXHAUSTED_IDLE` / `IDLE` (queue empty)\n1475\t5. `STOPPED`\n1476\t\n1477\t**4. Test worker filter**\n1478\t\n1479\tWorkers whose IDs match patterns like `test-*`, `claude-test-*`, `nonexistent-*`, `needle-test` should be hidden by default (togglable).\n1480\t\n1481\t**5. Productivity panel** (new tab/section in web dashboard)\n1482\t\n1483\t```\n1484\t┌─ Productivity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n1485\t│ Confirmed live on 2026-07-20:\n1617\t\n1618\t- On `ex44` (this machine), `~/.needle/config.yaml` has `fabric.enabled: true` with\n1619\t  `endpoint: http://localhost:3000/api/events` — but nothing listens on `ex44:3000`\n1620\t  (`fabric` isn't even installed on this host: `which fabric` → not found; `ss -tlnp`\n1621\t  shows no listener on 3000/4317/4318). Every event POST from `ex44`'s NEEDLE workers\n1622\t  has been silently failing (2s timeout, non-fatal to NEEDLE) since this config was\n1623\t  written — `ex44`'s worker activity has never been visible in any FABRIC dashboard.\n1624\t- On `lab`, FABRIC is deployed and (nominally) watches `lab`'s own\n1625\t  `~/.needle/logs/` only. So even when `lab`'s instance is healthy, it only ever\n1626\t  shows half (or less, as more hosts are added) of the actual fleet.\n1627\t- Compounding this: `lab`'s `fabric-web.service` has itself been down since\n1628\t  2026-07-09 (11 days, confirmed via `systemctl --user status`), and something else\n1629\t  (the unrelated `vista` app, also listening on port 3000 on `lab`) has been silently\n1630\t  squatting the port that `tailscale serve` proxies to — so the tailnet URL in\n1631\t  FABRIC's own README currently serves VISTA's page, not FABRIC's, with no visible\n1632\t  error (HTTP 200 both for `/` and for `/api/health`, which VISTA also happens to\n1633\t  implement with a different, non-FABRIC response shape). This class of failure is\n1634\t  already tracked in `bf-4grhf` (dashboard down) and `bf-18ib2` (its sibling failure,\n1635\t  the `fabric-prune.service` tar-archiving job, has failed nightly for ~2 months and\n1636\t  the watched logs directory has grown to the point the whole disk is now 96% full,\n1637\t  20GB free of 444GB). Those two beads cover *fixing the current instance*; this ADR\n1638\t  is about the *topology* those fixes should land into.\n1639\t\n1640\tPut together: the single-host, per-host-config architecture means (a) FABRIC never\n1641\thad fleet-wide visibility in the first place — the `ex44` half of the fleet was\n1642\talways dark — and (b) because only one instance exists and nothing external verifies\n1643\tit, an outage of that one instance goes unnoticed for as long as 11 days. Fixing\n1644\ttoday's specific outages (bf-4grhf, bf-18ib2) without addressing the topology just\n1645\trestores a single point of failure that is already known to be silently blind to\n1646\tpart of the fleet.\n1647\t\n1648\t### Decision\n1649\t\n1650\tAdopt the OTLP push model FABRIC's own README already documents as\n1651\t\"recommended for multi-host or production\" as the canonical wiring, instead of the\n1652\tper-host `localhost:3000` HTTP POST config:\n1653\t\n1654\t- Designate exactly one FABRIC instance (the `lab`-hosted one, reachable over\n1655\t  Tailscale) as the fleet's canonical collector.\n1656\t- Every NEEDLE host (starting with `ex44`) sets\n1657\t  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://<lab-tailscale-address>:4318` and\n1658\t  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf` (or the gRPC :4317 equivalent) instead\n1659\t  of relying on `fabric.enabled`/`endpoint` pointing at `localhost`. NEEDLE's `otlp`\n1660\t  feature already exists and needs no rebuild — this is a config change only.\n1661\t- FABRIC's own `NeedleEvent` schema and Prometheus metrics (`docs/schema.md`,\n1662\t  `docs/metrics.md`) gain a `host` label/field so events and metrics from different\n1663\t  machines remain distinguishable in one dashboard (workers on different hosts can\n1664\t  otherwise collide on the same worker-name conventions).\n1665\t- Because a single collector instance now carries the whole fleet's observability\n1666\t  instead of just one host's, its own liveness stops being a \"nice to have\" and\n1667\t  becomes load-bearing — this makes the existing outage beads (bf-4grhf, bf-18ib2)\n1668\t  higher-priority than they already are, and motivates adding an independent,\n1669\t  identity-verifying watchdog for that one instance (filed separately below rather\n1670\t  than folded into this ADR, to keep this decision scoped to topology).\n1671\t\n1672\t### Alternatives Considered\n1673\t\n1674\t1. **Fix `ex44`'s config to POST at `lab`'s Tailscale IP over HTTP instead of\n1675\t   localhost, keep the HTTP POST model.** Simplest one-line fix, but couples every\n1676\t   host's NEEDLE install to remembering and hand-editing an IP/hostname per machine,\n1677\t   has no batching, and is exactly the config style that already silently drifted\n1678\t   (nobody noticed `ex44` was pointed at `localhost` until this audit). Rejected as a\n1679\t   permanent fix, though it's a fine stopgap.\n1680\t2. **Run an independent `fabric-web` instance on every NEEDLE host.** Guarantees each\n1681\t   host's dashboard reflects that host's workers with no network dependency, but\n1682\t   directly contradicts FABRIC's purpose (\"what is each worker doing *across all\n1683\t   workers*\") — you'd need to check N separate dashboards to see the whole fleet, and\n1684\t   memory/disk/CPU overhead is paid N times over for a tool whose own resource\n1685\t   footprint is already under active investigation (bf-4grhf). Rejected.\n1686\t3. **Central OTLP collector (chosen).** One dashboard, one instance to keep healthy,\n1687\t   matches the multi-host guidance FABRIC's README already gives, no rebuild needed\n1688\t   on the NEEDLE side. Trade-off: the collector becomes a single point of failure for\n1689\t   fleet-wide visibility, which is why liveness verification for that one instance\n1690\t   becomes more important, not less, after this change.\n1691\t\n1692\t### Consequences\n1693\t\n1694\t- **Positive:** one dashboard shows the true state of the whole fleet (`ex44` +\n1695\t  `lab`, and any future host) instead of silently showing only whichever host\n1696\t  happens to be configured correctly; matches the architecture FABRIC's own docs\n1697\t  already recommend for this situation; no NEEDLE-side rebuild required.\n1698\t- **Negative:** the `lab`-hosted collector becomes load-bearing for observability\n1699\t  into `ex44` as well as `lab` — its uptime now matters fleet-wide, not just\n1700\t  locally, which raises the stakes on the existing outage/prune beads and on adding\n1701\t  external liveness verification (tracked as a separate bead below).\n1702\t- **Follow-up work required:** update `ex44`'s (and any future host's)\n1703\t  `~/.needle/config.yaml` or environment to point at the `lab` OTLP endpoint; add a\n1704\t  `host` label to `NeedleEvent`/Prometheus metrics so multi-host data doesn't\n1705\t  collide; both filed as beads referencing this ADR.\n1706\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e123db54-4f9a-4b44-94e5-55fc2c11bd26","uuid":"249f7644-14af-4cae-a570-34fc5ac35ba1","timestamp":"2026-07-24T12:22:20.314Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/coding/FABRIC/docs/plan.md","content":"# FABRIC Implementation Plan\n\n**Flow Analysis & Bead Reporting Interface Console**\n\n## Overview\n\nFABRIC is a live display for NEEDLE worker activity. It parses NEEDLE's logging output and renders it in real-time as either a TUI (terminal) or web dashboard.\n\n## Goals\n\n1. **Live Display**: Real-time visualization of NEEDLE worker activity\n2. **Dual Interface**: TUI for terminal users, web app for browser users\n3. **Stateless**: Reads and displays - no storage or persistence\n\n## Data Flow\n\n```\nNEEDLE Workers → ~/.needle/logs/ → FABRIC → Live TUI or Web Dashboard\n```\n\nFABRIC continuously tails NEEDLE's output and updates the display in real-time.\n\n## Input: NEEDLE Log Format\n\nFABRIC expects structured JSON log lines from NEEDLE:\n\n```json\n{\"ts\":1709337600,\"worker\":\"w-abc123\",\"level\":\"info\",\"msg\":\"Starting task\",\"task\":\"bd-xyz\"}\n{\"ts\":1709337601,\"worker\":\"w-abc123\",\"level\":\"debug\",\"msg\":\"Tool call\",\"tool\":\"Read\",\"path\":\"/src/main.ts\"}\n{\"ts\":1709337605,\"worker\":\"w-abc123\",\"level\":\"info\",\"msg\":\"Task complete\",\"duration_ms\":5000}\n```\n\n### Parsed Structure\n```typescript\ninterface LogEvent {\n  ts: number;\n  worker: string;\n  level: 'debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error';\n  msg: string;\n  [key: string]: any;  // Additional fields\n}\n```\n\n## Default Source\n\nFABRIC watches the directory `~/.needle/logs/` by default and tails every NEEDLE\nper-worker JSONL file concurrently. NEEDLE writes one JSONL per worker session\nnamed `{worker_id}-{session_id}.jsonl` (e.g. `alpha-d6288428.jsonl`). New files\nthat appear while FABRIC is running are hot-added without restart.\n\n```\n~/.needle/\n├── config.yaml                   # NEEDLE configuration\n├── logs/                         # FABRIC watches this directory\n│   ├── alpha-d6288428.jsonl      # one file per (worker, session)\n│   ├── bravo-44c92b93.jsonl\n│   └── ...\n├── state/                        # Runtime state\n├── cache/                        # Cached data\n└── README.md\n```\n\nThere is no consolidated `workers.log` — FABRIC must scan the directory and\ntail every matching file. (See Phase 8 for the fix to the original single-file\ntail bug.)\n\n## Output: Live Displays\n\n### TUI Mode (`fabric tui`)\n\nLive terminal dashboard that continuously updates:\n\n- **Worker Grid**: Real-time status of all active workers\n- **Log Stream**: Scrolling log output as events arrive\n- **Detail Panel**: Focus on a specific worker's activity\n\nFeatures:\n- Auto-updates as new log ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │     │\n│      │  │ 14:32:07  INFO   Edit src/auth/login.ts                   │   │     │\n│      │  │ 14:32:01  INFO   Read src/auth/types.ts                   │   │     │\n│      │  │ 14:31:55  DEBUG  Analyzing dependencies...                │   │     │\n│      │  │ 14:31:47  INFO   Glob **/*.ts (23 files)                  │   │     │\n│      │  │ 14:31:42  INFO   Starting task bd-1847                    │   │     │\n│      │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │     │\n│      │                                                                   │     │\n│      └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │\n│                                                                                 │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n## Intelligence Features\n\nFABRIC goes beyond simple log display with these intelligent features:\n\n### 1. Stuck & Loop Detection\n\nAutomatically detect when a worker is spinning its wheels:\n- No meaningful progress for N minutes\n- Repeating the same tool calls (Read → Edit → Read → Edit on same file)\n- Retrying failed operations repeatedly\n\nSurfaces problems immediately without users having to watch logs constantly.\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  ⚠️  STUCK DETECTED                                                │\n│                                                                     │\n│  w-alpha appears stuck (same file edited 4x in 6 minutes)          │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Pattern detected:                                                  │\n│    14:31:07  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"add validation\"                 │\n│    14:33:12  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"fix validation\"                 │\n│    14:35:18  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"update validation\"              │\n│    14:37:24  Edit src/auth.ts  →  \"refactor validation\"            │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Suggestion: Worker may be in a fix-break cycle                    │\n│                                                      [Inspect]      │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n**Loop Detection Patterns:**\n- Same file edited 3+ times in 5 minutes\n- Same Grep/Glob pattern executed repeatedly\n- Alternating Read/Edit on same file without progress\n- Retry count exceeding threshold\n\n---\n\n### 2. Live Inline Diff View\n\nWhen a worker calls `Edit`, render the actual diff inline with syntax highlighting:\n\n```\n14:32:07  w-alpha  INFO  Edit src/auth/login.ts\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  @@ -12,7 +12,9 @@                                                  │\n│                                                                     │\n│    import { User } from './types';                                  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  - function login() {                                               │\n│  + async function login(): Promise<User> {                          │\n│      const user = await authenticate();                             │\n│  -   return user;                                                   │\n│  +   if (!user) throw new AuthError('Invalid credentials');         │\n│  +   return sanitizeUser(user);                                     │\n│    }                                                                │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n**Implementation:**\n- Parse `old_string` and `new_string` from Edit tool call logs\n- Generate unified diff format\n- Syntax highlight based on file extension\n- Collapsible in log stream, expandable on click\n\n---\n\n### 3. Cross-Reference Hyperlinking\n\nEvery entity in logs becomes a clickable/navigable link:\n\n| Entity | Action |\n|--------|--------|\n| Bead ID (`bd-1847`) | Show all events across all workers for this bead |\n| File path (`src/auth.ts`) | Show all operations on this file |\n| Worker name (`w-alpha`) | Jump to worker detail view |\n| Timestamp | Anchor link for sharing/bookmarking |\n| Error code | Show all occurrences of this error |\n\n```\nActivity Stream\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ 14:32:07  [w-alpha]  INFO  Edit [src/auth/login.ts] for [bd-1847] │\n│           ─────────        ──── ───────────────────     ─────────  │\n│           clickable        tool      clickable          clickable  │\n│                                                                     │\n│ Clicking bd-1847 shows:                                            │\n│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │\n│ │ All events for bd-1847 \"Implement auth flow\"                │    │\n│ │                                                             │    │\n│ │ 14:29:00  w-alpha   Assigned task                          │    │\n│ │ 14:29:05  w-alpha   Glob **/*.ts                           │    │\n│ │ 14:30:12  w-alpha   Read src/auth/types.ts                 │    │\n│ │ 14:31:47  w-alpha   Read src/auth/login.ts                 │    │\n│ │ 14:32:07  w-alpha   Edit src/auth/login.ts                 │    │\n│ │ ...                                                         │    │\n│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n**TUI:** Tab/Enter to follow links, Backspace to go back\n**Web:** Standard hyperlinks with browser history\n\n---\n\n### 4. Worker Collision Detection\n\nReal-time detection when workers operate on overlapping concerns:\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  ⚡ COLLISION DETECTED                                              │\n│                                                                     │\n│  w-alpha and w-bravo are both modifying:                           │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌───────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┐       │\n│  │ File              │ w-alpha          │ w-bravo          │       │\n│  ├───────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────┤       │\n│  │ src/auth/login.ts │ Edit (line 45)   │ Edit (line 52)   │       │\n│  │ src/auth/types.ts │ Read             │ Edit (line 12)   │       │\n│  │ src/api/routes.ts │ -                │ Edit (line 88)   │       │\n│  └───────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────┘       │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Risk: Merge conflicts, duplicated work                            │\n│  Duration: Overlapping for 2m 34s                                  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  [View w-alpha]  [View w-bravo]  [View Diff]  [Dismiss]            │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n**Detection Logic:**\n- Track file → worker mapping in memory\n- Alert when same file has Edit from multiple workers within time window\n- Severity levels: Read/Read (info), Read/Edit (warn), Edit/Edit (critical)\n\n---\n\n### 5. Session Replay\n\nRecord sessions and play them back with timeline scrubbing:\n\n```\n┌─ FABRIC REPLAY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                                     │\n│  Session: 2026-03-02_14-20-00 (duration: 25m 34s)                  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ◀◀  ◀  ▶▶  ▶▶▶   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━●━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━   [2x]        │\n│  rew play pause ff            ↑                      speed         │\n│                          14:32:07                                   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │ Workers at 14:32:07                                         │   │\n│  │                                                             │   │\n│  │ ● w-alpha    Running   bd-1847  (2m 34s elapsed)           │   │\n│  │ ● w-bravo    Running   bd-1852  (1m 12s elapsed)           │   │\n│  │ ○ w-charlie  Idle      -        (completed bd-1845)        │   │\n│  │ ● w-delta    Starting  bd-1849  (just assigned)            │   │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Events at this moment:                                            │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │ ▶ 14:32:07  w-alpha   Edit src/auth/login.ts               │   │\n│  │   14:32:05  w-bravo   Read src/validators/index.ts         │   │\n│  │   14:32:04  w-delta   Starting task bd-1849                │   │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  [j/k] Frame step  [Space] Play/Pause  [←/→] Seek  [q] Exit        │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n**Features:**\n- Playback speeds: 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x\n- Click timeline to jump to any point\n- Frame-by-frame stepping (j/k or arrow keys)\n- Keyboard shortcuts for common actions\n- Export replay as shareable link or file\n\n**Implementation:**\n- Events are already timestamped in logs\n- Replay = render events progressively based on timestamps\n- No additional storage needed\n\n---\n\n### 6. Smart Error Grouping\n\nDon't scatter errors through the log stream. Group and contextualize them:\n\n```\n┌─ Errors (3 unique, 5 total) ───────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─ API Rate Limit ──────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │\n│  │  Occurrences: 2                                               │ │\n│  │  Workers: w-alpha, w-bravo                                    │ │\n│  │  First: 14:31:07  Last: 14:31:12  (5s span)                  │ │\n│  │                                                               │ │\n│  │  Context:                                                     │ │\n│  │    Both workers were making parallel Grep calls during        │ │\n│  │    search phase. Context] │ │\n│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─ FileNotFoundError occurrence count and time span\n- Auto-detect likely cause from preceding events\n- Link to similar past errors (if pattern matching enabled)\n- One-click to see full stack trace and surrounding Conversation Transcript View\n\nShow the actual Claude conversation—prompts and responses—not just tool calls. Tool calls are symptoms; the conversation is the substance.\n\n```\n┌─ Conversation: w-alpha ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─ System ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ You are working on bd-1847: Implement authentication flow    │  │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─ Assistant ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ I'll start by understanding the existing auth structure.     │  │\n│  │ Let me examine the current implementation.                   │  │\n│  │                                                              │  │\n│  │ [Tool: Glob **/*.ts in src/auth/]                           │  │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─ Tool Result ────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ Found 4 files: login.ts, types.ts, middleware.ts, utils.ts  │  │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─ Assistant ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │ Good, there's an existing auth module. Debug reasoning failures, understand worker logic, learn from good decisions.\n\n---\n\n### 12. retry_count INTEGER\n);\n\n-- Error history for Recovery Playbook\nCREATE TABLE error_history (\n  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n  session_id TEXT,\n  worker_id TEXT,\n  error_type TEXT,\n  error_message Extract error signature (type, message pattern, file pattern)\n2. Search historical session logs for similar errors\n3. Find subsequent events that resolved the error\n4. Rank by similarity and success rate\n5. Present as actionable suggestions\n\n**Error matching:**\n- Exact match: same error type and message\n- Pattern match: similar error type, related files\n- Semantic match: similar context (same task type, same module)\n\n**Feedback loop:**\n- Mark resolution as successful/failed\n- Improves future recommendations\n- Build organizational knowledge base\n\n**Why valuable:** Institutional memory. Don't repeat mistakes. Accelerate debugging. Workers (and humans) learn from past sessions.\n\n---\n\n### 18. Focus Mode with Pinning\n\nPin specific workers, tasks, or files. Everything else fades away:\n\n```\n┌─ FABRIC (Focus Mode) ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                                     │\n│  📌 Pinned: w-alpha, bd-1847                    [Exit Focus Mode]   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─ w-alpha on bd-1847 \"Implement auth flow\" ───────────────────┐  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  Status: ● Running (8m 34s)     Cost: $1.82                  │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  Progress                                                     │  │\n│  │  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━●━━━━━━━━━━━━  ~70% complete       │  │\n│  │  Research → Implementation → [Testing]                        │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Activity (filtered to pinned only)                                │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  14:32:07  Edit src/auth/login.ts                            │  │\n│  │            ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │  │\n│  │            │ - function login() {                        │   │  │\n│  │            │ + async function login(): Promise<User> {   │   │  │\n│  │            └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  14:32:01  Read src/auth/types.ts                            │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  14:31:55  Thinking: \"Now I need to implement the token     │  │\n│  │            validation. I'll create a new middleware...\"       │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  │  14:31:47  Glob **/*.ts → 23 files                           │  │\n│  │                                                               │  │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │\n│  Other activity (3 workers, muted)              [Show All]         │\n│  ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n**Pinning modes:**\n- Pin worker: Show only that worker's activity\n- Pin task (bead): Show all workers working on that task\n- Pin file: Show all operations on that file\n- Pin multiple: Combine any of the above\n\n**Keyboard shortcuts:**\n- `p` - Toggle pin mode\n- `P` - Clear all pins\n- Click/Enter on item while in pin mode adds to pins\n- `Esc` - Exit focus mode\n\n**Visual treatment:**\n- Pinned items: Full color, full detail\n- Unpinned items: Grayed out, collapsed, or hidden\n- Muted activity bar at bottom shows unpinned worker count\n\n**Presets:**\n- Save pin configurations as named presets\n- Quick switch: `>focus alpha` or `>focus auth-task`\n\n**Why valuable:** Reduce noise. Follow what matters. Deep focus on one task without distraction. Scales from \"show me everything\" to \"show me just this.\"\n\n---\n\n## CLI Interface\n\n```bash\n# TUI - live terminal dashboard\nfabric tui                              # Read from ~/.needle/logs/\nfabric tui --source /path/to/logs/      # Read from specific path\nfabric tui --worker w-abc123            # Filter to one worker\n\n# Web - live browser dashboard\nfabric web                              # Serve on http://localhost:3000\nfabric web --port 8080                  # Custom port\nfabric web --source /path/to/logs/      # Read from specific path\n\n# Simple log streaming (parsed + formatted, also live)\nfabric logs                             # Stream parsed logs to stdout\nfabric logs --level error               # Filter by level\nfabric logs --worker w-abc123           # Filter by worker\n```\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         FABRIC How many beads did they complete today? Which workers completed the most? Which projects got the most work done?\n\nThe live view (Phases 1–8) answers \"what is happening *right now*?\" — it shows NEEDLE state, heartbeats, active files, stuck detection. But it does not answer the retrospective question: *how much did the fleet actually accomplish?*\n\n#### The Problem\n\nWhen a user opens the dashboard and sees 40 workers all showing `EXHAUSTED_IDLE`, the dashboard appears to say \"nothing is happening.\" The correct interpretation is \"the fleet finished all available work.\" There is no way to tell from the current UI whether the workers completed 200 beads or 0.\n\nSimilarly, when workers are active, the worker card shows an event count (e.g., \"134,572 events\") but event count is an implementation detail, not a productivity signal. A worker that spent an hour stuck in a loop produces thousands of events and zero completions.\n\n#### Data Sources\n\nTwo data sources combine to answer the productivity question:\n\n**1. NEEDLE log events** (already ingested by FABRIC):\n\n| Event | What it signals |\n|-------|----------------|\n| `bead.claim.succeeded` | Worker started working on a bead; record start time |\n| `outcome.classified` with `outcome: success` | Agent exited cleanly; bead likely done |\n| `bead.released` with `reason: release_success` | NEEDLE confirmed the bead was closed; **this is the completion signal** |\n| `bead.released` with `reason: release_failure` | Worker dropped the bead without completing it |\n\nThe current `beadsCompleted` counter in `store.ts` only fires on a legacy `bead.completed` event that modern NEEDLE workers do not emit. The counter must be updated to fire on `bead.released` with `reason: release_success`.\n\n**2. Bead JSONL files** (not currently read by FABRIC):\n\nEach workspace has a `.beads/issues.jsonl` file. Closed beads carry:\n- `id` — bead identifier (prefix encodes the project, e.g. `kt-*` = kalshi-tape, `bf-*` = multi-project global)\n- `close_reason` — often contains the worker name (`\"Completed by worker claude-code-glm-4.7-india\"`)\n- `closed_at` — ISO timestamp of completion\n- `assignee` — the worker that held the bead\n\nReading these files unlocks project-level breakdown without requiring NEEDLE to emit workspace context in its log events.\n\n#### UI Changes Required\n\n**1. Fleet summary bar** (top of dashboard, always visible)\n\n```\n┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  3 WORKING  ·  7 SELECTING  ·  24 EXHAUSTED  ·  53 beads today  ·  0 stuck  │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nOne line. The single most important at-a-glance view. Replaces having to count individual worker cards.\n\n**2. Worker card enrichment**\n\nEach worker card should show beads completed (not event count) and, when `WORKING`, the current bead ID:\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  claude-code-glm-4.7-india  WORKING  │\n│  bead: bf-5r22                       │\n│  31 completed  ·  last: 2m ago       │\n└─────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n**3. Worker sort order**\n\nWorkers should sort by operational importance, not alphabetically:\n1. `WORKING` (doing something right now)\n2. `SELECTING` / `CLAIMING` (about to do something)\n3. `BOOTING` / `CLOSING`\n4. `EXHAUSTED_IDLE` / `IDLE` (queue empty)\n5. `STOPPED`\n\n**4. Test worker filter**\n\nWorkers whose IDs match patterns like `test-*`, `claude-test-*`, `nonexistent-*`, `needle-test` should be hidden by default (togglable).\n\n**5. Productivity panel** (new tab/section in web dashboard)\n\n```\n┌─ Productivity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ It shows what NEEDLE is doing, detects problems, and helps you understand your workers.\n\n---\n\n**Status**: Phases 1–9 complete.\n**Last Updated**: 2026-05-26\n\n## ADR-1: 2026-07-20 — Centralize FABRIC as a Multi-Host OTLP Collector\n\n### Context\n\nFABRIC's stated purpose (README, `docs/plan.md` Overview) is to be the observability\nlayer for *all* NEEDLE worker activity: \"What is each worker doing right now? ...\nacross all workers?\" In practice, on this workspace's actual infrastructure, NEEDLE\nworkers run on at least two independent hosts — this server (`ex44`, the primary\nHetzner box) and the `lab` server (100.81.129.38) — per `CLAUDE.md`'s Rust\nbuild/NEEDLE notes (\"NEEDLE workers on both servers inherit this behavior\ntransparently via PATH\") and this repo's own multi-host README section\n(\"Option 2: OTLP (recommended for multi-host or production)\").\n\nFABRIC itself, however, is only deployed on one host (`lab`), and each host's NEEDLE\ninstall is wired independently via the config-based HTTP POST option\n(`fabric.enabled: true`, `endpoint: http://localhost:3000/api/events` in\n`~/.needle/config.yaml`) rather than the OTLP option the README already recommends\nfor this exact situation. Confirmed live on 2026-07-20:\n\n- On `ex44` (this machine), `~/.needle/config.yaml` has `fabric.enabled: true` with\n  `endpoint: http://localhost:3000/api/events` — but nothing listens on `ex44:3000`\n  (`fabric` isn't even installed on this host: `which fabric` → not found; `ss -tlnp`\n  shows no listener on 3000/4317/4318). Every event POST from `ex44`'s NEEDLE workers\n  has been silently failing (2s timeout, non-fatal to NEEDLE) since this config was\n  written — `ex44`'s worker activity has never been visible in any FABRIC dashboard.\n- On `lab`, FABRIC is deployed and (nominally) watches `lab`'s own\n  `~/.needle/logs/` only. So even when `lab`'s instance is healthy, it only ever\n  shows half (or less, as more hosts are added) of the actual fleet.\n- Compounding this: `lab`'s `fabric-web.service` has itself been down since\n  2026-07-09 (11 days, confirmed via `systemctl --user status`), and something else\n  (the unrelated `vista` app, also listening on port 3000 on `lab`) has been silently\n  squatting the port that `tailscale serve` proxies to — so the tailnet URL in\n  FABRIC's own README currently serves VISTA's page, not FABRIC's, with no visible\n  error (HTTP 200 both for `/` and for `/api/health`, which VISTA also happens to\n  implement with a different, non-FABRIC response shape). This class of failure is\n  already tracked in `bf-4grhf` (dashboard down) and `bf-18ib2` (its sibling failure,\n  the `fabric-prune.service` tar-archiving job, has failed nightly for ~2 months and\n  the watched logs directory has grown to the point the whole disk is now 96% full,\n  20GB free of 444GB). Those two beads cover *fixing the current instance*; this ADR\n  is about the *topology* those fixes should land into.\n\nPut together: the single-host, per-host-config architecture means (a) FABRIC never\nhad fleet-wide visibility in the first place — the `ex44` half of the fleet was\nalways dark — and (b) because only one instance exists and nothing external verifies\nit, an outage of that one instance goes unnoticed for as long as 11 days. Fixing\ntoday's specific outages (bf-4grhf, bf-18ib2) without addressing the topology just\nrestores a single point of failure that is already known to be silently blind to\npart of the fleet.\n\n### Decision\n\nAdopt the OTLP push model FABRIC's own README already documents as\n\"recommended for multi-host or production\" as the canonical wiring, instead of the\nper-host `localhost:3000` HTTP POST config:\n\n- Designate exactly one FABRIC instance (the `lab`-hosted one, reachable over\n  Tailscale) as the fleet's canonical collector.\n- Every NEEDLE host (starting with `ex44`) sets\n  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://<lab-tailscale-address>:4318` and\n  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf` (or the gRPC :4317 equivalent) instead\n  of relying on `fabric.enabled`/`endpoint` pointing at `localhost`. NEEDLE's `otlp`\n  feature already exists and needs no rebuild — this is a config change only.\n- FABRIC's own `NeedleEvent` schema and Prometheus metrics (`docs/schema.md`,\n  `docs/metrics.md`) gain a `host` label/field so events and metrics from different\n  machines remain distinguishable in one dashboard (workers on different hosts can\n  otherwise collide on the same worker-name conventions).\n- Because a single collector instance now carries the whole fleet's observability\n  instead of just one host's, its own liveness stops being a \"nice to have\" and\n  becomes load-bearing — this makes the existing outage beads (bf-4grhf, bf-18ib2)\n  higher-priority than they already are, and motivates adding an independent,\n  identity-verifying watchdog for that one instance (filed separately below rather\n  than folded into this ADR, to keep this decision scoped to topology).\n\n### Alternatives Considered\n\n1. **Fix `ex44`'s config to POST at `lab`'s Tailscale IP over HTTP instead of\n   localhost, keep the HTTP POST model.** Simplest one-line fix, but couples every\n   host's NEEDLE install to remembering and hand-editing an IP/hostname per machine,\n   has no batching, and is exactly the config style that already silently drifted\n   (nobody noticed `ex44` was pointed at `localhost` until this audit). Rejected as a\n   permanent fix, though it's a fine stopgap.\n2. **Run an independent `fabric-web` instance on every NEEDLE host.** Guarantees each\n   host's dashboard reflects that host's workers with no network dependency, but\n   directly contradicts FABRIC's purpose (\"what is each worker doing *across all\n   workers*\") — you'd need to check N separate dashboards to see the whole fleet, and\n   memory/disk/CPU overhead is paid N times over for a tool whose own resource\n   footprint is already under active investigation (bf-4grhf). Rejected.\n3. **Central OTLP collector (chosen).** One dashboard, one instance to keep healthy,\n   matches the multi-host guidance FABRIC's README already gives, no rebuild needed\n   on the NEEDLE side. Trade-off: the collector becomes a single point of failure for\n   fleet-wide visibility, which is why liveness verification for that one instance\n   becomes more important, not less, after this change.\n\n### Consequences\n\n- **Positive:** one dashboard shows the true state of the whole fleet (`ex44` +\n  `lab`, and any future host) instead of silently showing only whichever host\n  happens to be configured correctly; matches the architecture FABRIC's own docs\n  already recommend for this situation; no NEEDLE-side rebuild required.\n- **Negative:** the `lab`-hosted collector becomes load-bearing for observability\n  into `ex44` as well as `lab` — its uptime now matters fleet-wide, not just\n  locally, which raises the stakes on the existing outage/prune beads and on adding\n  external liveness verification (tracked as a separate bead below).\n- **Follow-up work required:** update `ex44`'s (and any future host's)\n  `~/.needle/config.yaml` or environment to point at the `lab` OTLP endpoint; add a\n  `host` label to `NeedleEvent`/Prometheus metrics so multi-host data doesn't\n  collide; both filed as beads referencing this ADR.\n","numLines":1706,"startLine":1,"totalLines":1706}}}
